correctness.rationale: Pavlík's interval description gives one vertex per cube face and one edge per cover; the cube realization supplies the required existence. A nonempty face is a ternary word, so without the empty-face pole the graph is a product of three-vertex paths with distance 2a+b. The pole is adjacent precisely to the zero-free words, at distance f(u)+1 from u. Any geodesic either avoids it or uses it once, giving the minimum of the two stated costs. Equivalently the nonempty-pair metric is n+1−e−|a−c−1|, so equality with n+1 requires e=0 and a=c+1. Every nonpole with a fixed coordinate has a partner made by reversing one sign, freeing every other fixed coordinate, and fixing all free coordinates; the two poles partner each other. This proves all eccentricities, including n=1. The four ordered coordinate multiplicities are 2,4,1,2; deleting the 3^n diagonal pairs, halving the ordered count and adding the empty-face shells gives the enumerator, and degree-one coefficients agree with the edge count. The mean correction is 2E[(C−A+1)_+]. Only A−C≤0 contributes, and the single-coordinate exponential moment at (log 2)/2 is (6+2√2)/9, establishing the stated bound for sampling with replacement. An independently written vertex-set-inclusion graph and exhaustive BFS reproduced the metrics and all six listed diametral counts in dimensions 1–6 (/workspace/branches/independent_replay.py, cube()). The packaged checker was read but not run. The finite reproduction is not the all-n proof.

value.rationale: A single additional face vertex changes typical distances by a term linear in dimension relative to the coordinatewise product, yet every vertex has the same maximal eccentricity. Exact all-distance and diametral-pair data for this natural combinatorial polytope family, together with a quantitative mean estimate, make the metric useful beyond face counting or a small-dimensional observation.
